components-accordion-card.name: BpAccordionCard
components-accordion-card.description:
- Only one expanded card should be visible at a time in a section.
- Property values are shown in collapsed mode only; hide them in expanded mode.
- The optional radio button is for mutually exclusive accordion card selection.
- Pass `tag` and `headerAction` to show optional header slots; omit to hide them.
- `headerAction` is hidden when `disabled`; omit it for disabled/read-only rows.
- Bottom action buttons are optional when expanded (for example in wizards).
- Expand/collapse is one keyboard focus stop on the title trigger; the chevron toggles on click
  but stays out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
- Expanded panel landmarks use a stable `useId()` suffix so multiple cards on a page stay unique.

Stack multiple cards per Figma Accordion group:
- Sole section on the page: `BpStack space="100"` around cards.
- Multiple sections on the page: `BpStack space="200"` with `BpText type="section-title"` and
  `className="bp-accordion-cards--seamed"` on the card stack wrapper.

components-breadcrumbs.name: BpBreadcrumbs
components-breadcrumbs.description:
Use breadcrumbs at the top of content areas, especially deeply nested pages, to give users
context for what they're seeing and a way to navigate back up the page hierarchy.

Guidelines:
  - All crumbs other than the current page are clickable and should navigate to a parent page.
  - Breadcrumbs scroll with the entire page.
  - For paths deeper than 3 levels, the first and last level are visible. The rest is
    available from a menu triggered by an ellipsis button.

The overflow menu is rendered in a RAC `Popover` which handles:
- Outside-click dismissal
- Escape key dismissal
- Viewport-aware positioning

components-button.name: BpButton
components-button.description:
Buttons trigger actions and must clearly convey intent, hierarchy, and state.

Labels:
- Use a verb or verb phrase in sentence case.
- Keep text short and on one line—no wrapping or truncation.

Hierarchy:
- Primary: Solid; main action; one per view.
- Secondary: Outline/flat; supporting actions.
- Tertiary/Icon: Low emphasis; for contextual actions.
- Maintain consistent hierarchy across flows.

Placement:
- Dialogs/panels: Primary on the left; secondary after.
- Wizards/multi-action layouts: Primary on the right; secondary before.

Size & layout:
- Use predefined sizes only.
- Buttons in a row share width (based on longest label).
- Minimum width: 152px.
- No custom sizing or spacing.

Accessibility:
- Icon buttons should always include an \`aria-label\`.

components-chart-bar.description:
Blueprint Bar Chart (`Bar chart` / `Chart - ready to use ❇️` Chart=Bar / Stacked bar).

Vertical bars over labeled x-axis categories, on the chart
background. One series renders plain bars; two or more stack within each bar,
matching the Figma rule that all bars stack if any one does.

Pointer hover and keyboard exploration show the chart tooltip: a compact
category and value readout for a single series, or the titled per-series
breakdown when stacked. Tab focuses the chart's keyboard-help string, then
arrow keys (and Home/End) move between categories and Escape clears.

Bars always start at zero, so there is no `yDomain` — use `yMax` to pin the
scale. Prototype-grade only: no clustering, dual axes, or brushing.

Best when ~5 or more categories make the comparison worthwhile; for ~2–3
values without axes, use `BpComparisonChart` instead.

components-chart-donut.description:
Blueprint Donut Chart (`Donut chart ❇️`).

SVG donut chart with single-ring and two-ring (concentric) layouts,
optional center content, and three size variants.

Segments start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise. Tab focuses the chart's
keyboard-help string. For two-ring charts, Down enters on the outer ring and
steps inward, Up steps back out, and both clamp at the outermost and
innermost ring; Left and Right move through the selected ring's segments.
Single-ring charts keep using all arrow keys. Segment navigation wraps around
the ring. Escape clears the active readout.

Figma Content variants map to props as follows:
- "One level"            → `segments` only, no `innerSegments`
- "Two levels"           → `segments` + `innerSegments`
- "Two levels with total"→ `segments` + `innerSegments` (semantically the inner
                           ring represents a total or secondary breakdown)
- "No content"           → omit `centerValue`, `centerUnit`, `centerLabel`

Figma pairs Content with Size: two-ring charts are large only, and the small
(80 px) chart carries no center content.

Segment colors are passed explicitly as part of `BpDonutSegment` so callers
control the chart palette directly. Use semantic chart tokens so colors
respond to theming. When color has no data meaning, assign `--chart-9`,
`--chart-2`, `--chart-4`, `--chart-7`, `--chart-3`, `--chart-brand-13`,
`--chart-6`, `--chart-1`, `--chart-brand-12`, then `--chart-brand-16`.

Blueprint Horizontal Bar Row — one row of a horizontal bar chart.

Stack compact rows in a card for distributions; use `density="full"` for
icon + title + summary metric rows (Pre-dev Horizontal chart).

Choose `density` by the space available; use 5 or fewer full rows per card.
Every row in one compact series shares the same chart color — the rows

`role="meter"` value — no keyboard point traversal. Accessibility comes from
`aria-valuenow` / `min` / `max` (and the visible label / `meterAriaLabel`).
Apps that stack several rows rely on normal document order between them.

components-chart-line.name: BpLineChart
components-chart-line.description:
Blueprint Line Chart — library-owned data contract for prototypes and dashboards.

Line charts show a value over time; the x axis is time. Keep to ~10 series or
fewer for legibility.

Each series carries `points` of `{ x, y }` with `x` in epoch milliseconds, so
samples sit at their own timestamps and irregular sampling stays honest. Ticks
land on calendar boundaries and labels scale to the range ("4:00 AM", "May 15",
"May 2026", "2026") while the hover readout names the full date and time. Mark
forecast data with `projectedFromX`.

Figma `Chart - ready to use ❇️` Line variants (Line, Multi line, and their
projected-segment forms) are decorative mocks only. Map those instances to
this component with real or sample timestamped `series` data.

Prototype-grade linear scales and multi-series polylines only.
Zoom, brush, or dense telemetry: compose `BpChartFrame` with an app-owned plot.

Pointer hover and keyboard exploration snap to a sample time and draw the
Figma “Chart cursor” — a vertical reference line anchoring a readout tooltip
to that x-axis position — plus a point per series. Tab focuses the chart's
keyboard-help string, then left/right arrows (and Home/End) move between
sample times; Escape clears. The tooltip is visual-only and the live region
announces the active readout.

With multiple series, Down steps from the all-series view into each series in
turn and Up steps back out, so keyboard users can narrow to one line without
the legend. Hovering a line or legend entry, or focusing a series, keeps that
line in its series color and renders the other lines with `--chart-disabled`.

components-chat-panel.description:
Blueprint chat panel shell (Figma node `1:3458`).

Empty state guidance:
- Pass welcome/empty layouts through `emptyState`.
- Do not wrap empty-state layouts in `BpChatConversation`; that component is tuned for
  message transcripts and applies built-in conversation spacing.

Resize handle: pass `dragHandleProps={{ onPointerDown }}` (and optional `onKeyDown`) from the
parent; keep panel width in parent state. Use pointer capture + `pointermove` /
`pointerup` on `window`, clamp width, and update `aria-valuenow` / min / max on the handle
while dragging. With `onPointerDown` / `onKeyDown`, the handle gets `bp-chat-panel__drag-handle--interactive`
so `cursor` and `touch-action` apply only when resize is wired up.

dragHandleProps.description:
Forwarded to the drag handle. When you pass `onPointerDown` and/or `onKeyDown`, the handle
is exposed as a vertical `role="separator"` with a default `aria-label` (override with
`aria-label`), and gets `bp-chat-panel__drag-handle--interactive` plus `data-interactive` so
resize affordances (cursor, touch-action) apply. For live resize, also set `aria-valuenow`,
`aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` from the parent while width changes.

`role`, `aria-*`, pointer/click handlers, etc.) are stripped so callers cannot create a
focusable `aria-hidden` region or conflicting roles.

components-dropdown.name: BpDropdown
components-dropdown.description:
Blueprint Dropdown (Figma node `85088:11341`).

- Use when users pick from a known list in a form. Do not use for commands (`BpActionMenu`).
- `variant="field"` for standard forms; `variant="underline"` for dense layouts and filter
  rows. Pass `label` as a plain string so the trigger has an accessible name. Do not mix
  both variants on the same form without intent.
- Underline variant renders the label inline before the value (`Label: value`).
- Single select closes the menu after one choice; multi select keeps the menu open while
  toggling checkboxes. Use `actionMode` when changes should apply only on Apply.
- Multi-select defaults to `multiValueDisplay="chips"` (removable chips with `+N` overflow).
  Opt into `multiValueDisplay="summary"` for a short label or `{count} selected` on one row.
- Do not use `disabled` for read-only display — use `readOnly` when the value must stay
  visible but not editable.
- Use `loading` when options depend on async data. Use `hasError` / `messageType="warning"`
  for validation and non-blocking guidance (do not combine error and warning).
- Add `searchable` when there are more than 10 options. Show `showSelectAll` only when
  relevant and the list has 6 or more items.
- Match dropdown width to the grid and expected content length. Keep copy in sentence case.
- Clicking outside an open single-select dropdown closes it.
- Keyboard: Space, Enter, or Arrow Up/Down on the trigger opens the menu and
  moves focus to the first item (or search field when `searchable`). Arrow Up/Down
  navigate items, Escape closes, Home/End jump to ends.
- Split trigger (clear button or chip display): the caret button is the labelled
  control for the field label and the keyboard entry to open the menu.

primitives through `actions`.

components-key-value-pair.name: BpKeyValuePair
components-key-value-pair.description:
Blueprint key value pair (Figma node `7759:11932`).
https://www.figma.com/design/gHULaEjWAA66bkWHfWIenp/%F0%9F%92%8E-Pre-dev-components?node-id=7759-11932

Used to display a label and its associated value, typically as a read-only property listing.
When multiple key value pairs are grouped together, compose them inside {@link BpKeyValuePairStack }.

[Usage guidelines](https://www.figma.com/design/gHULaEjWAA66bkWHfWIenp/%F0%9F%92%8E-Pre-dev-components?node-id=7995-18739)

**When to use**
- Present read-only metadata, attributes, or summary information about an object or entity.
- Users need to scan and compare properties quickly in a structured layout.
- Detail panels, sidebars, cards, or summary sections where property listings are needed.

**When not to use**
- Editable fields — use form inputs instead.
- Tabular data with multiple rows of the same properties — use a table.
- Single, standalone metrics or KPIs — use a stat or metric component.
- Long-form descriptive content — use a text block or content area.

**Value types**
- **Text** (`type="text"`): Simple string or numeric values such as names, dates, IDs, or descriptions.
  Keep values concise; if text exceeds two lines, consider truncation with a tooltip or an expandable pattern.
- **Link** (`type="key-link"` / `type="value-link"`): When the key or value references a navigable resource,
  such as a related record, URL, or linked entity. Ensure the link label conveys the destination.
- **Status** (`type="status"`): State or condition such as success, warning, or error.
  Always pair the status with a visible label; do not rely on icon alone to convey meaning.
- **Icon** (`type="icon"`): When a visual symbol reinforces or replaces a simple text value,
  such as a platform logo or file type. Always provide an accessible label alongside the icon (`value` text).
- **List** (`type="list"`): Multiple related items such as tags, assigned users, or categories.
  Keep list items short; overflow collapses via {@link BpInlineList}.
- **Graph** (`type="bar-chart"`, `type="horizontal-chart"`, `type="sparkline-chart"`): Small inline visualization,
  such as a sparkline, mini bar chart, or progress indicator. Do not use for complex or interactive charts.
  Ensure the graph includes sufficient context, such as a label or value annotation.

**Figma type mapping**

| Figma type | `type` prop | Required props |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | `text` (default) | `label`, `value` |
| Status | `status` | `label`, `value`, optional `statusTone` |
| Icon | `icon` | `label`, `value`, `icon` |
| Bar chart | `bar-chart` or `horizontal-chart` | `label`, `chartValue`, optional `value` caption |
| Sparkline chart | `sparkline-chart` | `label`, optional `value` caption, optional `sparklineData`, or `chart` |
| List | `list` | `label`, `items` |
| Key link | `key-link` | `label`, `href`, optional `description` |
| Value link | `value-link` | `label`, `value`, `href` |

Sparkline defaults are decorative. Pass `sparklineData` for a simple numeric series, or `chart` for app-owned chart components.

for information and success. Pass `"off"` when the notification is already
represented in a labeled list.

components-search.description:
Overview
- Search allows users to type a query, then view results in an adjacent part of the UI.
- Searches don’t require a dedicated “Search” button. A new search is triggered each
time the user enters a character. Start searching on the first character.
- By default, search can either be collapsed into a search icon or presented as a
complete search field.

Expandable search
- Displayed as an icon by default.
- Expands with a click.
- The ‘x’ icon closes the field and clears the typed text.
- When the field is empty, clicking outside closes the field.

Non-expandable search
- Displayed by default as an open field
- The user must focus the field, then type.

Placeholder text
- Search fields display “Search” placeholder text by default. Designers can customize this
message using the pattern “Search {objects}” if the UI doesn’t make it clear what the input
searches.

components-simple-filters.description:
Simple filters bar (Figma node `86422:42107`).

Renders a horizontal surface with a filter icon and "Filters" heading on the
leading side, a wrapping flex row of filter controls in the center, and an
optional Reset button on the trailing side.

Usage:
- Use simple filters at the top of a page to set the scope of an entire page via a series of dropdowns.
- Use up to 4 dropdowns.
- Use to switch among views, select a specific object to view, or change the type of content visible on the page.
- Pass `BpDropdown variant="underline"` controls as `children`.
- Provide `onReset` to reveal the Reset button; omit it to hide the button.
- The bar stretches to fill its container width. Set an explicit width on the
  parent when you need to constrain it.
- Do not mix `BpDropdown variant="field"` controls on the same bar — use
  underline only in filter rows.

components-slider.name: BpSlider
components-slider.description:
Sliders provide a visual indication of adjustable content,
where the user can increase or decrease the value by moving the
handle along a horizontal track.

Usage guidelines:
- Defining a step (e.g., 1, 5, 10) controls the increment by which the value updates.
- Step values accept whole numbers or decimals up to two decimal points.
- Dragging the slider handle manually updates the value.
- Clicking anywhere on the horizontal track updates the value.
- Writing a number in the range value line above the slider updates the slider.
- The slider text label indicates the value the slider is hovering over.
- Range values are used to describe the range in numbers.
- Specifying an appropriately large step ensures usability for ranges greater than 1,000 (e.g., a range of 1–1,000,000 that uses a step of 10,000).
- Do not use for ranges that are too small i.e. 1-3.

components-tab-group.name: BpTabGroup
components-tab-group.description:
Use to group different but related content, allowing users to navigate views without leaving the page.

Figma: Tab group ❇️ (`82036:57204`), Tab (`82036:57250`).

Guidance:
- Use at least two tabs with short, specific labels (1-2 words).
- One tab is active at a time and should remain selected when users return within the same session.
- Do not use tabs for external navigation or side-by-side comparison tasks.
- Use the `horizontalResizing` prop to control how tabs size themselves.
- The tab group controls all the elements under it on the page, replacing all of the content underneath the tab bar when a new tab is selected.
- General tab groups always span the full width of their container.
- Card tab groups typically span the full width of the card, except in cases where the card spans a very wide area,
  which would make the tab interaction awkward.
- Tab overflow occurs when the number of tabs exceeds the available horizontal space. Overflow scroll controls
  appear automatically; set `horizontalResizing` to `"hug"` so tabs keep their natural width.
- Set `reorderable: true` on tabs that users should drag into a new order, and handle `onTabsReorder`.
  While dragging, the lifted tab follows the pointer and neighboring tabs slide aside to show the drop gap.
  Reorderable tabs also move with Ctrl+Shift+ArrowLeft or Ctrl+Shift+ArrowRight when focused.
- When tabs exceed the available width, previous/next scroll buttons appear and the tab list
  scrolls horizontally (including via mouse wheel).
- Pass `tablistAriaLabel` with a specific name for what the tabs control (for example,
  "Report sections") instead of relying on the generic default.
- Pass `children` for the host-owned panel. Switch panel content based on the selected tab
  (for example, a single table keyed by `value`).
- Use `selectionMode="strict"` when a disabled tab should stay highlighted under a controlled `value`.

**BpTab** fields:
- `id`: Unique tab identifier used for selection.
- `label`: Visible tab label content.
- `disabled`: Disables tab interaction when true.
- `icon`: Optional Blueprint icon name or SVG icon component.
- `count`: Optional numeric/text count shown next to label.
- `reorderable`: When true, this tab can be dragged to a new position.
  Tabs without `reorderable` and disabled tabs act as barriers: reorderable tabs cannot move past them.
  While dragging toward a blocked slot, the fixed tab that prevents the drop shows disabled styling.
- `removable`: Shows a close control at the right edge; visible on hover and when the tab is selected.
  Reorderable tabs show a drag handle on hover and while pressed.
  The handle is decorative; keyboard reorder does not depend on it.
- `removeAriaLabel`: Screen reader label for the remove action.

components-tag.name: BpTag
components-tag.description:
Tags visually label items with small amounts of information (1-2 words) or the item’s status,
usually with keywords that help organize and categorize the items.

**Guidelines**

Use of color
- Prefer to use the existing color combinations when possible, even when using labels other than the pre-defined set.
- You may use custom colors if the predefined set of colors don't meet your needs.
- If you need to communicate that something is off or disabled, use the "Grey" variant.
- Don't use tags for the standard set of notification statuses. Use notification icons + text instead.

Labeling
- Aim to use only 1-2 words.
- Use sentence style capitalization—only capitalize the first letter of the first word.
- Don’t use punctuation within tags.
- Avoid verb forms that imply actionability or interactivity. Tags should reflect state or context, not suggest that the user can perform an action.
- OK: “Coming soon,” “New,” “Pending”
- Not OK: “Activate,” “Approve,” “Retry”

Pre-defined tags
There are four pre-defined tags, each associated with a distinct color:
- “Private preview” tag: Use the "Blue" variant. Private use to specific (invited or opt-in) customers.
- “Preview” tag: Use the "Blue" variant. Ability to use new service with the understanding that there may be bugs, and further refinement of features are to be expected. Feature/service is exposed to all users in the UI with a “Preview” flag.
- “Coming soon” tag: Use the "Purple" variant. Place next to placeholder or empty content to indicate that new functionality or content is coming soon. Avoid using this tag unless there are near-future PM plans to introduce the functionality.
- “Best” tag: Use the "Yellow" variant. Place next to the superior option among a list of choices. For example, the best hardware configuration in the upgrade advisor in the Keystone service.

components-text-area.name: BpTextArea
components-text-area.description:
Use a text area when the expected user input is more than a few words and could span multiple lines.
It supports all the same states and functionality as text input except for the password functionality.
Text area has several unique functionalities not included in the default text input, like the resize handle and character counter, both are optional.

Guidelines:
- Align the text area width to the grid columns.
- Allow the size of the text area to reflect the length of the content you expect the user to enter and the size of the layout it sits in.
- The resize handle has no effect on the width of the text area container, it only affects the height. The user can manipulate the text area height by making it longer or shorter.
- Min height should be 40px. Define the max height according to the expected length of text.
- Text area label should be written in sentence case.
- Placeholder text inside the text area should be written in sentence case and is optional.
- In uncontrolled mode, `defaultValue` is initial-only. To reset the rendered value,
  either control `value` or remount with a different `key`.

components-tooltip.description:
Blueprint Tooltip (Figma node `84524:56926`).

Gives brief, contextual help on hover or keyboard focus: the name of a
control that has no visible label, the full text of a truncated label, or a
short clarification that helps someone decide. Keep copy short and scannable.

Required field information, validation errors, long or multi-step
instructions, and anything else critical belong in helper text, an inline
message, a popover, or a dialog — a tooltip hides them behind hover. When a
label reads unclearly, rewrite the label instead of explaining it here.
Tooltip content must stay presentational. Use a popover when people need to
focus or interact with content such as a link, button, or removable chip.

Accessibility comes from react-aria-components `TooltipTrigger` and
`Tooltip`: `aria-describedby` wiring, hover delay, focus-visible open,
Escape dismiss, and repositioning when the preferred side doesn't fit.
